central_claim.note: Conservative half of C1 for both hesitancy and boosters; that liberals are low in hesitancy or likely boosted regardless of climate is not stated. 'Moderates' is the paper's own framing.

evidence.note: Online survey, US, March to April 2023 (E1) without the nonprobability convenience sample or Qualtrics Panels; final N = 683 (E2) without the 1,777 collected and 970 screened out.

key_findings.note: Hesitancy half of F1 (positive main associations with vaccine and booster hesitancy, p.7); the vaccination and boosting half is not stated here.
Conservative half of the hesitancy interaction; the liberal half is in another entry.
Booster-status interaction is significant (p.10), without its shape or direction.
Liberal half of the hesitancy interaction (low regardless of climate, p.10).

scope_and_limits.note: Unmeasured regional factors such as population density may be associated with the findings: the consequence of the zip-code proxy (p.10).

theoretical_positioning.note: Extends prior work by testing the interaction; does not say the prior literatures each studied orientation or climate, so no T1 (the quote does, the claim does not).

interlocutor_claim.note: Builds on the conservatism-hesitancy and uptake association; quote p.10 cites refs 6, 7, 10, 19.
